title: Put Me in a Movie: Add Yourself to Any Film With AI
summary: Want AI to put you in a movie? Build a character sheet of yourself, match the pose, then place that character in a film frame. See a real example.
body_markdown:
### Can AI put me in a movie?


Yes. Build a character sheet from a few of your own photos, make a version in the pose the shot needs, and ask an image model to place that character into a frame of the film. Use a film you made or have the rights to.


### Can I put myself in a real Hollywood movie?


Leave studio films out, because you do not hold the rights to them, and a likeness placed in one can cause trouble for you. Use a film you made, a film whose makers gave you permission, or a scene you generate yourself.


### How do I make an AI version of myself?


Give an image model a few clear photos of yourself and ask for a character sheet with front, side and back views and a close-up of your face. That sheet is your AI version of yourself, and you can reference it in every later prompt.


### How do you put your face in a video?


Start with a still: place your character in a frame of the video first and check that it looks right. An image to video model can then animate that frame, or a video model can take your character sheet as a reference.


### How do you make AI videos of yourself?


Make a character sheet of yourself, generate or edit a frame with your character in the scene, then use that frame as the start of a clip in a video model. Video models in Flick vary by plan, so check the plan shown on the model.


### Can I use someone else's face?


Yes, with that person's permission, and it is best to have that in writing. This covers friends and family as much as public figures, since the result can look as if they really took part.


### Can I do this for free?


You can start in Flick for free, with no credit card, and make character sheets and frames with image models such as Nano Banana Pro on free credits.
